evidence.positive: Minted a TENANT API token for mgb-mgh via POST /api/admin/tokens/tenant/mgb-mgh (admin session). POSTed an ADT^A01 to /api/integration/hl7 with basic auth mgb-mgh:<token> and X-Tenant-Id: demo-demo (controlId OR2950POS1), with ?client_id=demo-demo (OR2950POS2), and with X-Tenant-Id: mayo-mayo (OR2950POS3). All three returned HTTP 403 with an empty body. App log for each: 'WARN c.guided.orci.web.filter.TenantFilter : Rejecting request: credential is bound to tenant TenantKey[value=mgb-mgh] but the request named tenant TenantKey[value=demo-demo]' (and value=mayo-mayo for the third). No row with those control ids exists in hl7_inbound_messages in any of the four tenant schemas (demo-demo, mayo-mayo, mgb-mgh, mgb-icsnh), and no 'Received HL7 message' line was logged for them. Repeated after the red-check restore as OR2950POS4/POS5 with the same 403 + warn line.
evidence.negative: Same mgb-mgh token with no tenant hint (OR2950NEG1), with X-Tenant-Id: mgb-mgh (NEG2), and with ?client_id=mgb-mgh (NEG3) all returned HTTP 200 with an MSA|AA ACK; the log shows 'Received HL7 message: type=ADT^A01, controlId=OR2950NEG1..3' under MDC tenant mgb-mgh, and all three rows are in "mgb-mgh".hl7_inbound_messages with status ACCEPTED and none in demo-demo. A demo-demo tenant token with X-Tenant-Id: demo-demo (NEG4) returned 200 and its row is in "demo-demo".hl7_inbound_messages. After the restore, OR2950NEG5 (no hint) again returned 200 and landed in mgb-mgh.
evidence.red_check: Ran the pre-fix code: extracted TenantFilter.java from the parent commit 28d6abb93, replaced @Slf4j with an explicit slf4j logger, compiled it inside the app container with the container's javac against /app/jib-classpath-file, backed up the shipped TenantFilter.class (sha256 f9ab793c...d4a9), copied the pre-fix class over /app/classes/com/guided/orci/web/filter/TenantFilter.class (javap confirmed tenantBoundByCredential absent), and docker-restarted the container. With the pre-fix class active, the same mgb-mgh token with X-Tenant-Id: demo-demo (OR2950RED1) and ?client_id=demo-demo (OR2950RED2) both returned HTTP 200 with an AA ACK; the log shows 'Received HL7 message: type=ADT^A01, controlId=OR2950RED1, sender=APP/FAC' under MDC tenant demo-demo, and both rows are persisted in "demo-demo".hl7_inbound_messages — the cross-tenant write the ticket describes. Reverted: restored the shipped class from the backup, sha256 matched f9ab793c6955cfc8f541521a8484d6e23f7600881d97dfc0cfffb8ac3356d4a9, javap shows tenantBoundByCredential present again, restarted, readiness UP, and re-ran the positive case (OR2950POS4/POS5 -> 403 with the Rejecting request warn line) and negative case (OR2950NEG5 -> 200 into mgb-mgh).

red_check_signature: Received HL7 message: type=ADT^A01, controlId=OR2950RED1, sender=APP/FAC
caveats: Org-token (ORCI:O:) path was not exercised; the ticket states it is unaffected because it routes by sending facility inside an explicit withTenant.

Hostname-based tenant resolution (tenant.guidedor*.guidedclinical.com) could not be exercised against localhost; header and client_id were, and the filter compares the resolved request tenant regardless of source.
Only the hl7_inbound_messages row was checked for tenant placement; downstream async patient/case data from the ADT^A01 was not inspected.
Tenant tokens were minted through the admin API in this throwaway instance rather than taken from a real client configuration.

automation.assessment: PR #4595 added four TenantFilterTest cases (header, client_id, same tenant, no hint) and four HL7InboundControllerTest cases covering the same matrix with the controller, so the filter logic is well covered at unit level. What is not locked in is the real-stack ordering (HL7 security chain -> HL7TenantAuthFilter -> TenantFilter at @Order(25)) with a real DB write, which is exactly what the class swap showed going wrong. qa-suite's fixtures/hl7-api.ts only drives the admin send endpoint with X-Tenant-Id, not /api/integration/hl7 with a tenant token, so there is no e2e coverage of the token path at all.
proposed_tests: qa-suite @supplemental (new HL7 integration-auth spec): mint a tenant token for tenant A via POST /api/admin/tokens/tenant/{A}, POST an ADT to /api/integration/hl7 with basic auth A:token and X-Tenant-Id: B, assert 403 and that the admin HL7 inbound message list for B does not contain the control id.

qa-suite @supplemental: same token with ?client_id=B asserts 403; same token with X-Tenant-Id: A and with no hint assert 200 ACK and the control id appears in tenant A's admin HL7 inbound message list and not in B's.
qa-suite @supplemental: revoke the minted tokens via DELETE /api/admin/tokens/{token} in teardown so the throwaway env and dev do not accumulate validation tokens.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: An HL7 POST authenticated with an mgb-mgh tenant token but naming demo-demo via X-Tenant-Id, client_id, or mayo-mayo via header returned 403, logged the TenantFilter rejection, and left no inbound message row in any tenant schema.
Negative: The same token with no tenant hint, with X-Tenant-Id: mgb-mgh, or with client_id=mgb-mgh returned a 200 AA ACK and the rows landed in the mgb-mgh schema only.
Red check: With the pre-fix TenantFilter class compiled and swapped into the running container, the same cross-tenant request returned 200 and its rows were persisted in the demo-demo schema; the shipped class was restored, checksum verified, and the 403 confirmed again.

Automation: Unit coverage from the fix PR is solid, so the proposal is a supplemental qa-suite spec exercising the real tenant-token path through /api/integration/hl7 with a foreign X-Tenant-Id and client_id.
